$comment: Which failure_taxonomy IDs a LegalityChecker can be held responsible for, and how to synthesise a trace that violates each one. A checker observes transactions in ORDER and carries no cycle information — the contract deliberately withholds timing, because timing is what SVA checks. So a checker cannot be graded on a tRCD violation, and asking it to would be demanding evidence it cannot have. This file records that split as data so it is reviewable rather than buried in a gate.
$split_rationale: TIMING_* and INIT_002 and DATA_002 are elapsed-time properties: they belong to Validation/sva. DATA_001 is a value comparison: it belongs to the scoreboard and its predictor. CSR_001 is register access semantics: it belongs to the register-map predictor gate. What remains are ordering and state properties, which are exactly what a transaction-level checker can see.

checkable.requirement: READ/WRITE issued to a bank that has no active row.
checkable.why: A CAS with no preceding ACTIVATE to that bank has no open row to address.

checkable.requirement: ACTIVATE issued to a bank that already has an active row without intervening PRECHARGE.
checkable.why: A second ACTIVATE to the same bank without a PRECHARGE between them.

checkable.requirement: REFRESH issued while one or more banks are still active (not precharged).
checkable.why: A REFRESH while bank 0 still has an open row.

not_checkable_here.why: elapsed-time properties; a checker sees order, not cycles
a value comparison against a predicted response
register access semantics, graded on the predictor

REF_001 needs the refresh request/ack stream and INIT_001 needs the init command stream; both are checkable in principle but the traces are synthesised on ddr_cmd, which carries neither. Add when those interfaces are monitored.
